newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler lays off 950 in Wisconsin due to strike.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler lays off 950 in Wisconsin due to strike.

text.p: As the strike at its Mound Road engine plant dragged into its 15th day Friday, Chrysler Corp. told about 950 workers not to report to work Monday at another engine factory in Kenosha, Wis.
The new layoffs brought the number of Chrysler workers idled by the strike to nearly 25,000 in the United States, Canada and Mexico.
Nearly 10,000 workers also remained idled Friday by two strikes at General Motors Corp. assembly plants in Pontiac, Mich., and Oklahoma City.
"It's the same-old same-old," Chrysler spokesman Dan Moore said of communications between bargainers for the automaker and United Auto Workers Local 51.
The two sides have not met face-to-face since about 1,856 workers walked out of the Mound Road plant just before midnight on April 9, although they continue to talk via telephone.

The union has demanded that Chrysler drop plans to shift drive shaft production to an outside supplier, a move it says will eliminate 250 jobs. But Chrysler has dug in on its position, saying it needs to remain flexible in its components purchases if it wants to stay competitive.

The strike has forced Chrysler to shut down its Jeep Grand Cherokee plant in Detroit, its large van plant in Windsor, Ontario, and plants that make Dodge Ram and Dakota pickup trucks in Warren, Mich., St. Louis and Lago Alberto and Saltillo, Mexico.

The Kenosha engine plant is idling more than half of its 1,760 workers because Chrysler is not producing the Jeep Grand Cherokees that use the in-line, six-cylinder engines it builds. Chrysler has enough of the six- and four-cylinder engines stockpiled to allow another Jeep plant in Toledo, Ohio, to continue operating.

Negotiations also continued Friday to resolve a three-day-old strike involving about 5,850 workers at Pontiac, which builds GM's popular full-size, extended-cab pickup trucks, and at Oklahoma City, where 3,500 workers halted production of Chevrolet Malibu and Oldsmobile Cutlass cars on April 4.
